body.statement: The map \(W\mapsto\theta(W,z)\), whose last coordinate is \(\mu_0=m_0\), is a bijection from \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{adm}}\) to all structural explanations of the four observed Gaussian snapshot laws. Equivalently, a raw candidate is compatible if and only if \(\rho(W)<1\), \(\operatorname{spec}(W)\cap(-\infty,0]=\varnothing\), and the Stein reconstruction satisfies \(E_W=C_0-T_W\succ0\). Global identification holds if and only if \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{adm}}\) is a singleton.
body.proof_tex:
First derive the observable restrictions from the structural model.  By \(\text{ass:linear-flow}\), \(\text{ass:initial-gaussian}\), \(\text{ass:common-measurement-noise}\), \(\text{ass:measurement-independence}\),
\[
 m_k=V^k(\mu_0-x^\star)+x^\star,
 \qquad
 C_k=V^k\Sigma(V^{\mathsf T})^k+E.
\]
Consequently the common noise cancels from adjacent differences and
\[
 H_j=V^j(\Sigma-V\Sigma V^{\mathsf T})(V^{\mathsf T})^j,
 \qquad
 d_j=V^j(V-I_p)(\mu_0-x^\star).
\]
It follows equation by equation that
\[
 VH_0V^{\mathsf T}=H_1,\quad VH_1V^{\mathsf T}=H_2,
 \quad Vd_0=d_1,\quad Vd_1=d_2,
\]
so every explanation supplies a raw candidate.

Necessity of the filters follows next.  A complex Schur triangularization of \(G\) makes \(\exp(hG)\) triangular with diagonal entries \(e^{hg}\), where \(g\) ranges over the eigenvalues of \(G\).  Thus \(\text{ass:hurwitz}\) gives \(\rho(V)<1\).  Moreover \(e^{hg}\) cannot lie on \(( -\infty,0]\): it is nonzero, and a negative real value would require \(\operatorname{Im}(hg)\equiv\pi\pmod {2\pi}\), contrary to \(\text{ass:alias-strip}\).  Finally,
\[
 \Sigma-V\Sigma V^{\mathsf T}=H_0,
\]
so uniqueness of the stable Stein solve gives \(T_V=\Sigma\), and then \(E_V=C_0-T_V=E\succ0\).

For sufficiency, fix \(W\in\mathcal F_{\mathrm{adm}}\).  Since \(\rho(W)<1\), the series
\[
 T_W=\sum_{j=0}^{\infty}W^jH_0(W^{\mathsf T})^j
\]
converges in every matrix norm and satisfies \(T_W-WT_WW^{\mathsf T}=H_0\).  It is positive definite because its first summand is \(H_0\succ0\).  It is unique: vectorization turns the homogeneous Stein equation into
\[
 (I_{p^2}-W\otimes W)\operatorname{vec}(T)=0,
\]
and every eigenvalue of \(W\otimes W\) is a product of two eigenvalues of \(W\), hence has modulus less than one.  Set \(E_W=C_0-T_W\), which is positive definite by membership in \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{adm}}\).  The Stein identity gives
\[
 WT_WW^{\mathsf T}+E_W=T_W-H_0+C_0=C_1.
\]
If \(\widetilde C_k=W^kT_W(W^{\mathsf T})^k+E_W\), then
\[
 \widetilde C_k-\widetilde C_{k+1}=W^kH_0(W^{\mathsf T})^k.
\]
The two raw congruences identify the right side successively with \(H_0,H_1,H_2\).  Since \(\widetilde C_0=C_0\), telescoping therefore yields \(\widetilde C_k=C_k\) for \(k=0,1,2,3\).

Stability implies \(I_p-W\) is invertible.  Put
\[
 x_W^\star=(I_p-W)^{-1}(m_1-Wm_0),\qquad \widetilde m_0=m_0,
 \qquad \widetilde m_{k+1}=W\widetilde m_k+(I_p-W)x_W^\star.
\]
Then \(\widetilde m_1=m_1\).  Moreover the increments obey
\[
 \widetilde m_{k+1}-\widetilde m_k=W(\widetilde m_k-\widetilde m_{k-1}).
\]
The raw equations \(Wd_0=d_1\) and \(Wd_1=d_2\) consequently imply, successively, \(\widetilde m_2=m_2\) and \(\widetilde m_3=m_3\).  Thus the reconstructed initial mean is necessarily \(\mu_0=m_0\).

It remains to justify the continuous-time coordinate and its uniqueness.  On the slit plane \(\mathbb C\setminus(-\infty,0]\), define \(\operatorname{Log}(W)\) by the holomorphic functional calculus.  Complex conjugation of the defining contour integral shows that it is real when \(W\) is real.  Spectral mapping gives
\[
 \operatorname{spec}(\operatorname{Log}W)
 =\{\log|w|+i\operatorname{Arg}(w):w\in\operatorname{spec}(W),\ -\pi<\operatorname{Arg}(w)<\pi\}.
\]
Hence \(G_W=h^{-1}\operatorname{Log}(W)\) is real, has spectrum in the required alias strip, and is Hurwitz because \(|w|<1\).  If another real logarithm \(L\) of \(W\) had all eigenvalues in the same open strip, then the scalar identity \(\operatorname{Log}(e^z)=z\) on that strip, composed through the holomorphic functional calculus, would give \(L=\operatorname{Log}(e^L)=\operatorname{Log}(W)\).  Thus no logarithm branch remains.

Now take \(X_0\sim\mathcal N(m_0,T_W)\), generate the deterministic affine trajectory with \((W,x_W^\star)\), and take mutually independent \(\mathcal N(0,E_W)\) measurement errors independent of \(X_0\).  The preceding identities show that every resulting marginal has exactly mean \(m_k\) and covariance \(C_k\).  Gaussian laws are determined by these two moments, so this construction reproduces all four observed laws.  Conversely, the necessity argument recovers every coordinate of any explanation from its \(W\).  Because \(\theta(W,z)\) includes \(W\) itself, the correspondence is injective as well as surjective.  The identified set is therefore exactly the image of \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{adm}}\), and global identification is equivalent to that fiber containing one element.
body.justification: The algebraic orthogonal fiber becomes scientifically meaningful only after stability, logarithm, Stein, and noise-positivity filters are jointly shown necessary and sufficient.
body.gap: Neither AaltoLamolineGoncalves2022 nor WangEtAl2024 characterizes the compatible level-covariance and continuous-time generator fiber when the same unknown positive-definite measurement covariance contaminates every snapshot.
body.consumer: The public \(\texttt{covar\_lin\_dyn}\) workflow can add joint calibration of \(E\) and an exact ambiguity certificate before interpreting a recovered interaction matrix.
